note: The 30 queries the rule-1 / reach / floor / cost audit runs on BOTH sides. Superset of the 3 sanity queries in bakeoff-queries.json, which are carried verbatim (positions 1-3) and asserted equal at load time by audit-run.js. Written for the audit, then frozen: no query was added, dropped or reworded after seeing a result, because a query set tuned against outcomes measures the tuner.

universes.corpus: all 2204 films. THE PRIMARY. bakeoff-queries.json says the dense side can only reach 1541; that stopped being true when build-index.py added the description-tier fallback, so both sides now see all 2204 and this is the honest shared universe.
universes.plotted: the 1541 films at or above the 1500-char plot floor. Secondary, kept so the like-for-like run against the older assumption still exists.

design.mood: a felt quality, no plot noun to grab. Where dense retrieval is expected to degenerate to title matching.
design.shape: the form of the story rather than its content.
design.setting: a place or period. Concrete, but a place is not an attribute in the 59-term vocabulary.
design.tone: register — irony, sincerity, dryness. The atlas vocabulary is strongest here.
design.concrete: names things that literally happen on screen. Where dense retrieval over plot text should win if it wins anywhere.
design.negation: carries a 'not'. One side has an operator for it and one cannot represent it at all.
design.quiet: aimed at the unfamous half of the corpus on purpose. A retriever that only knows canon should visibly fail these, and the fame audit reads them hardest.
design.exemplar: names a film as the example. query-parse.js has a code path for this; the dense side sees only a title string.
